1: Chief complaint: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
2: Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis
3: Plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air–fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm
4: Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum
